questions.label: Health data
questions.ask: Do customers store protected health information (PHI) in the product?
options: Yes, patient health information is core to the product
Only incidentally, such as in support messages
questions.fills: Template fit. No means a BAA is not needed; say so before drafting.
questions.codebase: Schema fields for patients, diagnoses, treatments or insurance IDs.

questions.label: Underlying agreement
questions.ask: Which agreement does this BAA attach to?
questions.fills: Cover: Agreement. Company, BAA Effective Date and signature block use the clickthrough model: Company is the company or person who accepts this BAA and the BAA Effective Date is the date Company first accepts.

questions.label: Relationship
questions.ask: Under HIPAA, what role do your customers usually have?
options: Covered Entity; we are their Business Associate
Business Associate; we are their subcontractor

questions.label: Breach notice
questions.ask: How quickly will you tell a customer about a breach after you find it?

questions.label: Designated Record Set
questions.ask: Do you keep PHI that is used to make decisions about patients, such as medical or billing records?

questions.label: Subcontracting
questions.ask: May you pass PHI to your own vendors?
options: Yes, as the standard terms allow

questions.label: Offshoring
questions.ask: May PHI be stored or handled outside the United States?
options: Yes, as the standard terms allow

questions.label: De-identification
questions.ask: May you de-identify PHI for your own use?
options: Yes, as the standard terms allow
Only for a named purpose (type it)

questions.label: Aggregation

options: Yes, as the standard terms allow
